claim: Manganese enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MEMRI) was applied for the first time to the eggs of domestic chicks.
source: Here, we applied for the first time manganese enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MEMRI), a functional imaging method, to the eggs of domestic chicks.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this is the first application of MEMRI to chick eggs.

claim: MEMRI revealed light-induced brain asymmetry by comparing embryonic brain activity in vivo of eggs that were stimulated by light or maintained in darkness.
source: We revealed light-induced brain asymmetry by comparing embryonic brain activity in vivo of eggs that were stimulated by light or maintained in the darkness.
evidence: The abstract states this as a primary finding of the study.

claim: Some of the molecular cues that specify the left-right axis of the body are guided by genes of the Nodal cascade.
source: Some of the molecular cues that specify the left-right axis of the body are guided by genes of the Nodal cascade (Halpern et al., 2003; Rogers et al., 2013; Ocklenburg and Güntürkün, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by three citations to prior research.

claim: Nodal cascade genes are involved in the establishment of the asymmetric morphology and positioning of the visceral organs.
source: These genes are involved in the establishment of the asymmetric morphology and positioning of the visceral organs (Ramsdell and Yost, 1998)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ramsdell and Yost, 1998.

claim: Nodal cascade genes produce a slight torsion of the embryo with the forehead pointing to the right.
source: These genes are involved in the establishment of the asymmetric morphology and positioning of the visceral organs (Ramsdell and Yost, 1998), but also produce a slight torsion of the embryo with the forehead pointing to the right.
evidence: This is stated as a known fact following discussion of Nodal cascade genes.

claim: Rightward spinal torsion occurs in all amniotes.
source: This rightward spinal torsion seems to occur in all amniotes (Zhu et al., 1999) including human embryos (Ververs and Hopkins, 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Zhu et al., 1999 and Ververs and Hopkins, 1994.

claim: The torsion is particularly prominent in birds.
source: The torsion is particularly prominent in birds.
evidence: This is stated as a comparative observation about birds relative to other amniotes.

claim: In most bird species, the head of the embryo is turned to the side, so that the left eye is completely occluded by the body, while the right eye faces the eggshell.
source: In most species, the head of the embryo is turned to the side, so that the left eye is completely occluded by the body, while the right eye faces the eggshell (see Figure 1a).
evidence: This anatomical observation is stated in text and illustrated in Figure 1a.

claim: Light stimulation passing through the eggshell and membranes reaches mostly the right eye.
source: Thus, light stimulation passing through the eggshell and membranes reaches mostly the right eye.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the asymmetric positioning of the embryo.

claim: Fibers coming from each eye decussate almost completely at the level of the optic chiasm.
source: Fibers coming from each eye decussate almost completely at the level of the optic chiasm.
evidence: This is stated as an established anatomical fact about avian visual pathways.

claim: In the thalamofugal pathway, visual fibers ascend contralaterally to the thalamus (nucleus geniculatus lateralis pars dorsalis, Gld) and from there mostly ipsilaterally to the visual Wulst.
source: In the thalamofugal pathway, they then ascend contralaterally to the thalamus (more precisely at the level of the nucleus geniculatus lateralis pars dorsalis, Gld) and from there mostly ipsilaterally to the visual Wulst (an avian equivalent of the primary visual cortex of mammals).
evidence: This describes the anatomical pathway of visual fibers in birds.

claim: The visual Wulst is an avian equivalent of the primary visual cortex of mammals.
source: In the thalamofugal pathway, they then ascend contralaterally to the thalamus (more precisely at the level of the nucleus geniculatus lateralis pars dorsalis, Gld) and from there mostly ipsilaterally to the visual Wulst (an avian equivalent of the primary visual cortex of mammals).
evidence: This is stated as an anatomical comparison between avian and mammalian brain structures.

claim: In chicks, a small portion of visual fibers called supraoptic decussation re-cross from the thalamus and innervate the contralateral side of the Wulst.
source: In chicks it has been shown that a small portion of visual fibers, so called supraoptic decussation, re-cross from the thalamus (Figure 1a) and innervate the contralateral side of the Wulst.
evidence: This anatomical feature is stated and illustrated in Figure 1a.

claim: Light stimulation in the embryo during embryonic days E17-18 is a sensitive period.
source: Following light stimulation in embryo during a sensitive period embryonic days E17–18 (Rogers and Deng, 1999)
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Rogers and Deng, 1999.

claim: Light stimulation in the embryo results in more projections from the left thalamus (receiving visual input from the right eye) than from the right thalamus to the right Wulst on post-hatching day 2.
source: Following light stimulation in embryo during a sensitive period embryonic days E17–18 (Rogers and Deng, 1999), however, in previous experiments it has been shown that light stimulation in the embryo result, on post-hatching day 2, in more projections from the left thalamus (receiving visual input from the right eye) than from the right thalamus to the right Wulst (Rogers and Deng, 1999)
evidence: This is a finding from previous research cited as Rogers and Deng, 1999.

claim: Paramagnetic manganese ions Mn2+ enter excitable cells via voltage-gated calcium channels.
source: Paramagnetic manganese ions Mn2+ enter excitable cells via voltage-gated calcium channels, and can be transported along axons and across synapses (Massaad and Pautler, 2011).
evidence: This mechanism is stated with a citation to Massaad and Pautler, 2011.

claim: Manganese ions can be transported along axons and across synapses.
source: Paramagnetic manganese ions Mn2+ enter excitable cells via voltage-gated calcium channels, and can be transported along axons and across synapses (Massaad and Pautler, 2011).
evidence: This property of manganese is stated with a citation to Massaad and Pautler, 2011.

claim: Changes in the regional contrast of magnetic resonance images induced by activity-dependent accumulation of manganese provide a means to map neuronal activation elicited by stimuli.
source: Hence, changes in the regional contrast of magnetic resonance images induced by activity-dependent accumulation of manganese provide a means to map neuronal activation elicited by stimuli (Lin and Koretsky, 1997)
evidence: This application of MEMRI is stated with a citation to Lin and Koretsky, 1997.

claim: Manganese accumulation can be used to trace axonal tracts.
source: Hence, changes in the regional contrast of magnetic resonance images induced by activity-dependent accumulation of manganese provide a means to map neuronal activation elicited by stimuli (Lin and Koretsky, 1997) and to trace the axonal tracts involved (Pautler et al., 1998; Van der Linden et al., 2007).
evidence: This application is stated with citations to Pautler et al., 1998 and Van der Linden et al., 2007.

claim: Manganese was administered to the embryos on E17 via the chorioallantoic membrane.
source: On E17 we administered manganese to the embryos via the chorioallantoic membrane.
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure used in the study.

claim: One group of embryos was incubated with light and the other was incubated in darkness immediately after manganese administration.
source: Immediately after, one group of embryos was incubated with light (light) and the other was incubated in the darkness (dark).
evidence: This describes the experimental design with two conditions.

claim: On E18 eggs were placed in the scanner and functional T1 maps were acquired.
source: On E18 eggs were placed in the scanner (MR) and functional T1 maps were acquired.
evidence: This describes the timing and method of data acquisition.

claim: Mn2+ is a paramagnetic ion and shortens the T1 of nuclear spins in brain tissue in a concentration-dependent manner.
source: Mn2+ is a paramagnetic ion and shortens the T1 of nuclear spins in brain tissue in a concentration-dependent manner.
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption as a property of manganese relevant to the imaging method.

claim: Blue-darker regions in T1 maps correspond to higher intracellular Mn2+ accumulation, and hence to increased neuronal activity.
source: Blue-darker regions correspond to higher intracellular Mn2+ accumulation, and hence to increased neuronal activity.
evidence: This interpretation of the imaging data is stated in the figure caption.

claim: The ANOVA revealed a significant main effect of brain region (F(2,32) = 3.693, p=0.036).
source: The ANOVA revealed a significant main effect of brain region (F(2,32) = 3.693, p=0.036)
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis.

claim: The ANOVA revealed a significant interaction between brain region and condition (F(2,32) = 4.274, p=0.023).
source: The ANOVA revealed a significant main effect of brain region (F(2,32) = 3.693, p=0.036) and a significant interaction between brain region and condition (F(2,32) = 4.274, p=0.023)
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis.

claim: The ANOVA revealed no significant main effect of condition (F(1,16) = 0.335, p=0.571).
source: while no significant main effect of condition (F(1,16) = 0.335, p=0.571).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis.

claim: A significant difference between conditions was found in the thalamus (t(16) = -2.710, pFDR = 0.045, d = -1.286), which showed higher manganese uptake/activity in the dark condition.
source: A significant difference between conditions was found in the thalamus (t(16) = -2.710, pFDR = 0.045, d = -1.286), which showed higher manganese uptake/activity in the dark condition (dark: mean -0.038 ± s.e.m. 0.006; light: -0.015±0.006).
evidence: This is a statistical result with specific values from the data analysis.

claim: No significant differences were found between conditions in the visual Wulst (t(16) = 1.280, pFDR = 0.329, d=0.607).
source: No significant differences were found between conditions in either the visual Wulst (t(16) = 1.280, pFDR = 0.329, d=0.607; dark: -0.007±0.005; light: -0.020±0.009)
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis.

claim: No significant differences were found between conditions in the optic tectum (t(16) = -0.148, pFDR = 0.884, d = -0.070).
source: No significant differences were found between conditions in either the visual Wulst (t(16) = 1.280, pFDR = 0.329, d=0.607; dark: -0.007±0.005; light: -0.020±0.009) or the optic tectum (t(16) = -0.148, pFDR = 0.884, d = -0.070; dark: -0.010±0.009; light: -0.009±0.006).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis.

claim: A significant right lateralization was detected in the thalamus in the dark group (t(7) = -6.090, p≤0.001, d = -2.153).
source: A significant right lateralization was detected in the thalamus in both groups (dark: t(7) = -6.090, p≤0.001 (uncorrected), d = -2.153
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis.

claim: A significant right lateralization was detected in the thalamus in the light group (t(9) = -2.419, p=0.039, d = -0.765).
source: A significant right lateralization was detected in the thalamus in both groups (dark: t(7) = -6.090, p≤0.001 (uncorrected), d = -2.153; light: t(9) = -2.419, p=0.039 (uncorr.), d = -0.765).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis.

claim: The visual Wulst was significantly right lateralized in the light group (t(9) = -2.383, p=0.041, d = -0.754).
source: The visual Wulst was significantly right lateralized in the light group (t(9) = -2.383, p=0.041 (uncorr.), d = -0.754)
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis.

claim: No significant lateralization emerged in the visual Wulst in the dark group (t(7) = -1.350, p=0.219, d = -0.477).
source: The visual Wulst was significantly right lateralized in the light group (t(9) = -2.383, p=0.041 (uncorr.), d = -0.754), but no significant lateralization emerged in the dark group (t(7) = -1.350, p=0.219, d = -0.477).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis.

claim: No significant lateralization was found in the optic tectum in the dark group (t(7) = -1.149, p=0.288, d = -0.406).
source: No significant lateralization was found in the optic tectum either of the groups (dark: t(7) = -1.149, p=0.288 (uncorr.), d = -0.406
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis.

claim: No significant lateralization was found in the optic tectum in the light group (t(9) = -1.493, p=0.170, d = -0.472).
source: No significant lateralization was found in the optic tectum either of the groups (dark: t(7) = -1.149, p=0.288 (uncorr.), d = -0.406; light: t(9) = -1.493, p=0.170 (uncorr.), d = -0.472).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis.

claim: A spontaneous (dark) as well as an induced (light) lateralization of brain activity was detected in the thalamofugal visual pathway (thalamus).
source: We detected a spontaneous (dark) as well as an induced (light) lateralization of brain activity in the thalamofugal visual pathway (thalamus)
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the statistical results.

claim: No lateralization nor any effect of light was observed in the optic tectum.
source: We detected a spontaneous (dark) as well as an induced (light) lateralization of brain activity in the thalamofugal visual pathway (thalamus); in contrast, no lateralization nor any effect of light was observed in the optic tectum (see Figure 1c).
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the statistical results, with reference to Figure 1c.

claim: After light stimulation the manganese accumulation revealed a right lateralized brain activity in the Wulst, congruent with increased activity from the left thalamus to the right Wulst (via the supraoptic decussation).
source: After light stimulation the manganese accumulation revealed a right lateralized brain activity in the Wulst, congruent with increased activity from the left thalamus to the right Wulst (via the supraoptic decussation).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results in the context of known anatomy.

claim: In the complete absence of visual stimulation (dark), a strong right lateralization was found in the thalamus.
source: Interestingly, however, in the complete absence of visual stimulation (dark), we found a strong right lateralization in the thalamus
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data.

claim: Light exposure seemed to reduce spontaneous asymmetry in the thalamus, as a result of light stimulation to the right eye that likely increased activity in the left thalamus.
source: light exposure seemed to reduce such spontaneous asymmetry, as a result of light stimulation to the right eye that likely increased activity in the left thalamus (due to complete decussation at the level of optic chiasm).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data based on known anatomy and the experimental manipulation.

claim: Manganese accumulation in the tissue seems to be directly linked to the promotion of the growth of the fibers along the supraoptic decussation from the left thalamus to the right Wulst.
source: Thus, manganese accumulation in the tissue seems to be directly linked to the promotion of the growth of the fibers along the supraoptic decussation from the left thalamus to the right Wulst.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mechanism underlying the observed results.

claim: Asymmetry in manganese accumulation can be interpreted as a result of prolonged neuronal stimulation under illumination compared to the dark condition.
source: Asymmetry in manganese accumulation can be interpreted as a result of prolonged neuronal stimulation under illumination compared to the dark condition.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mechanism underlying the observed asymmetry.

claim: Changes in cellular density may contribute to differential distribution of Mn.
source: Changes in cellular density may also contribute to differential distribution of Mn.
evidence: This is mentioned as an alternative possible mechanism.

claim: Within the temporal frame of the experiment, it is unlikely that altered cellularity is the main mechanism, as several-fold changes in cell density would be needed to explain the observed differences in T1.
source: However, within the temporal frame of the experiment, we deem it unlikely that altered cellularity is the main mechanism, as we should assume several-fold changes in cell density to explain the observed differences in T1.
evidence: This is a reasoning about why an alternative mechanism is unlikely.

claim: Light-induced region-specific changes in blood brain barrier permeability appear unlikely under the experimental conditions of this study.
source: Similarly, light-induced region-specific changes in blood brain barrier permeability appear unlikely under the experimental conditions of this study.
evidence: This is a statement about why another alternative mechanism is unlikely.

claim: Light stimulation during the sensitive window appears to be crucial in establishing brain asymmetry at the onset of life.
source: Light stimulation during the sensitive window appears to be crucial in establishing brain asymmetry at the onset of life.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Spontaneous lateralization of brain activity seems to be already present during embryonic development in the complete absence of external light stimulation.
source: However, spontaneous lateralization of brain activity seems to be already there during embryonic development in the complete absence of external light stimulation (for spontaneous lateralized activity soon after hatching, see Lorenzi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the dark condition results, with a citation to related work.

claim: A similar interplay between a genetically determined rightward torsion of the body and the resulting asymmetry in sensory stimulation may represent a general mechanism for brain asymmetry in all vertebrates, including humans.
source: It has been hypothesized that a similar interplay between a genetically determined rightward torsion of the body and the resulting asymmetry in sensory stimulation (even for other sensory modalities) may represent a general mechanism for brain asymmetry in all vertebrates, including humans (Rogers et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a hypothesis cited from Rogers et al., 2013.

claim: This new protocol of MEMRI allowed mapping in vivo in the embryo the lateralized pattern of brain activity at the early stages of brain development for the first time.
source: This new protocol of MEMRI allowed us for the first time to map in vivo in the embryo the lateralized pattern of brain activity at the early stages of brain development.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty and capability of the method.

claim: The MEMRI protocol could be further exploited to investigate early embryonic learning that occurs as a result of sensory stimulation through the egg before birth.
source: The MEMRI protocol here established could be further exploited to investigate early embryonic learning that occurs as a result of sensory stimulation through the egg before birth.
evidence: This is a statement about potential future applications of the method.

claim: Fresh fertilized eggs of the Aviagen Ross 308 strain (Gallus gallus domesticus) were used in the study.
source: Fresh fertilized eggs of the Aviagen Ross 308 strain (Gallus gallus domesticus; provider: Azienda Agricola Crescenti Brescia, Italy) were incubated in the laboratory under constant temperature and humidity in the complete darkness (37.7°C; 60%; incubator: FIEM MG140/200 Rural LCD EVO).
evidence: This describes the experimental subjects used in the study.

claim: Eggs were incubated under constant temperature (37.7°C) and humidity (60%) in complete darkness.
source: Fresh fertilized eggs of the Aviagen Ross 308 strain (Gallus gallus domesticus; provider: Azienda Agricola Crescenti Brescia, Italy) were incubated in the laboratory under constant temperature and humidity in the complete darkness (37.7°C; 60%; incubator: FIEM MG140/200 Rural LCD EVO).
evidence: This describes the incubation conditions for the eggs.

claim: On embryonic day 17 (E17), the eggshell was pierced in correspondence of the air sac.
source: On embryonic day 17 (E17), the eggshell was pierced in correspondence of the air sac.
evidence: This describes a step in the experimental procedure.

claim: 80 µl of manganese chloride (540 mM MnCl2 tetrahydrate) dissolved in phosphate-buffered saline was dropped on the chorioallantoic membrane.
source: 80 µl of manganese chloride (540 mM MnCl2 tetrahydrate, Sigma-Aldrich) dissolved in phosphate-buffered saline (0.1 M, pH = 7.4, 0.9% sodium chloride) were dropped on the chorioallantoic membrane.
evidence: This describes the manganese administration procedure with specific concentrations.

claim: After manganese injection, a group of 10 eggs were exposed to 17.30 hr of light (light group).
source: After manganese injection a group of 10 eggs were exposed to 17.30 hr of light (light group), by mean of a rectangular plastic translucent panel (36×38 cm2), with 15 LEDs (270 lm) homogeneously distributed on it placed on the roof of the incubator 15 cm above the eggs.
evidence: This describes the light exposure condition with specific parameters.

claim: Another group of eight eggs were incubated in the darkness (dark group).
source: Another group of eight eggs were incubated in the darkness (dark group).
evidence: This describes the dark control condition.

claim: On E18 each egg was placed inside a dark box and moved to the fridge (4°C) for 30 min to avoid any movement during scanning.
source: On E18 each egg was taken individually and randomly from one of the two incubators (light or dark), placed inside a dark box and moved to the fridge (4°C) for 30 min in order to avoid any movement during scanning.
evidence: This describes the preparation procedure before imaging.

claim: Sample size was determined based on previous experiments on newly hatched chicks.
source: Sample size was determined based on previous experiments on newly hatched chicks (Halpern et al., 2003).
evidence: This explains the rationale for the sample size with a citation.

claim: Images were acquired at 7 T on a Bruker Pharmascan with a 72 mm i.d. single-channel transmitter-receiver birdcage resonator.
source: Images were acquired at 7 T on a Bruker Pharmascan (https://www.bruker.com) with a 72 mm i.d. single-channel transmitter-receiver birdcage resonator.
evidence: This describes the imaging equipment used.

claim: Eggs were kept at 4°C in a temperature-controlled refrigerator for 20 min prior to acquisition to avoid artifacts caused by spontaneous movement of the chick embryo.
source: To avoid artifacts caused by spontaneous movement of the chick embryo, eggs were kept at 4°C in a temperature-controlled refrigerator for 20 min prior to the acquisition.
evidence: This describes a methodological step to prevent motion artifacts.

claim: Mild hypothermia ensured the immobilization of the chick embryo within the egg for about 30/45 min.
source: This ensured the immobilization of the chick embryo within the egg due to mild hypothermia for about 30/45 min.
evidence: This explains the effect of cooling on embryo movement.

claim: Regions of interest (ROIs) were selected from the two main visual pathways, the thalamo- and the tectofugal pathway blinded from the experimental condition.
source: Regions of interest (ROIs) were selected from the two main visual pathways, the thalamo- and the tectofugal pathway blinded from the experimental condition.
evidence: This describes the ROI selection procedure with blinding to reduce bias.

claim: For the thalamofugal visual pathway a portion of the dorsolateral thalamus and of the visual Wulst were selected, of which respectively three and two sections per each hemisphere were quantified.
source: For the thalamofugal visual pathway a portion of the dorsolateral thalamus and of the visual Wulst were selected, of which respectively three and two sections per each hemisphere were quantified.
evidence: This describes the specific ROIs and number of sections analyzed.

claim: For the tectofugal visual pathway only the optic tectum was selected, of which four sections per each hemisphere were quantified.
source: For the tectofugal visual pathway only the optic tectum was selected, of which four sections per each hemisphere were quantified.
evidence: This describes the specific ROIs and number of sections analyzed for the tectofugal pathway.

claim: ROIs were segmented manually on the first volume of the RARE-VTR dataset of each animal using the free software ITK-SNAP.
source: ROIs were segmented manually on the first volume of the RARE-VTR dataset of each animal using the free software ITK-SNAP (https://www.itksnap.org/; Yushkevich et al., 2006).
evidence: This describes the segmentation method and software used.

claim: Quantitative T1 maps were obtained by fitting the general signal recovery model in Matlab to produce voxelwise distributions of T1 relaxation time over the whole brain.
source: Quantitative T1 maps were obtained by fitting the general signal recovery model in Matlab (https://www.mathworks.com) to produce voxelwise distributions of T1 relaxation time over the whole brain.
evidence: This describes the data processing method for generating T1 maps.

claim: Lateralization index values ranged from 1 (brain activity present only in the left hemisphere) to –1 (brain activity present only in the right hemisphere).
source: Lateralization index values ranged from 1 (brain activity present only in the left hemisphere) to – 1 (brain activity present only in the right hemisphere).
evidence: This explains the interpretation of the lateralization index values.

claim: The difference in lateralization between the two experimental conditions for the three brain regions was tested with a repeated measurement ANOVA.
source: The difference in the lateralization between the two experimental conditions, for the three brain regions, was tested with a repeated measurement ANOVA, between-subjects factor 'condition' (two levels: light, dark), within-subject factor 'brain region' (three levels: Wulst, thalamus, optic tectum).
evidence: This describes the statistical test used for the main analysis.

claim: False discovery rate (FDR) was applied to correct for multiple comparisons.
source: False discovery rate (FDR) was applied to correct for multiple comparisons.
evidence: This describes the correction method for multiple comparisons.

claim: For post hoc analyses, one-sample two-tailed t-tests were used to compare lateralization indexes against the expected chance level (0).
source: For post hoc analyses, one-sample two-tailed t-tests were used to compare lateralization indexes against the expected chance level (0).
evidence: This describes the statistical test used for post hoc comparisons.

claim: Two-tailed independent samples t-tests were used to compare indexes between conditions.
source: Two-tailed independent samples t-tests were used to compare indexes between conditions.
evidence: This describes the statistical test used for between-condition comparisons.

claim: For every t-test the Cohen's d was calculated as a measure of the effect size.
source: For every t-test the Cohen's d was calculated as a measure of the effect size.
evidence: This describes the effect size measure reported.

claim: No correction for multiple comparisons was applied to the post hoc analyses.
source: No correction for multiple comparisons was applied to the post hoc analyses.
evidence: This describes a limitation of the post hoc statistical analyses.

claim: All analyses and the raincloud plot were performed using the software R.
source: All the analyses and the raincloud plot were performed using the software R (https://www.r-project.org/).
evidence: This describes the software used for statistical analysis and visualization.
